s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent painful skin lesions with ulceration and systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Painful pimple-like bumps on bilateral lower legs
Ulcers with central eschars and dusky gray borders
key_facts: Patient is a young black woman
Presented with chills and bilateral lower extremity swelling
Recent course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for MSSA
Medical history includes methimazole and atenolol
Pitting edema and multiple discrete round dry ulcers on lower legs
Laboratory tests show elevated CRP and ESR
Normal C3 and C4 complement levels
ANA titer 1:80
P-ANCA titer 1:20
Anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) titer 141 U
Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies level 120 U
Pathology shows lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with neutrophils and focal abscess
Special stains negative for organisms

raw.syndrome_frame: Recurrent painful skin lesions with ulceration and systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Painful pimple-like bumps on bilateral lower legs
Ulcers with central eschars and dusky gray borders

Presented with chills and bilateral lower extremity swelling
Recent course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for MSSA
Medical history includes methimazole and atenolol
Pitting edema and multiple discrete round dry ulcers on lower legs
Laboratory tests show elevated CRP and ESR

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated ANCA titer and presence of systemic inflammation

shortlist.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated MPO titer and presence of renal and skin involvement

shortlist.label: Erythema induratum
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent painful skin lesions with ulceration and systemic inflammation

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of neutrophilic infiltrate and vasculitis on pathology

shortlist.label: Cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of skin lesions and systemic inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with painful lesions, pitting edema, and multiple discrete round dry ulcers on the lower legs, along with laboratory tests showing elevated CRP and ESR, and pathology revealing lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with neutrophils and focal abscess, is most consistent with cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis. The presence of anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) titer 141 U and anti-SSA/Ro antibodies level 120 U also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and laboratory tests do not show granulomatous inflammation, which is a hallmark of granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

rejected.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated anti-MPO titer, the lack of renal involvement and the presence of skin lesions with lymphohistiocytic infiltrate suggest cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis rather than microscopic polyangiitis.

rejected.label: Erythema induratum
rejected.why: The patient's lesions do not have the characteristic features of erythema induratum, such as recurrent painful nodules on the calves.

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: While the patient's pathology shows lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with neutrophils, the clinical presentation and laboratory tests are more consistent with cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis.
